newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool indicator rises 4c to 598c/kg.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool indicator rises 4c to 598c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose 4.0 cents to 598 cents a kg clean on Thursday at sales in Sydney and Adelaide, Wool International (WI) said.
Merino fleece was mostly dearer, apart from the 19/20 micron categories which fell by 0.5 percent.
The 21/23m indicators were 1.5 percent dearer, 22m 0.5 percent dearer and 24m 1.5 percent dearer. The 25m class was up to 2.0 percent dearer, while 26m rose by up to 2.5 percent.
Merino skirtings of 19/20m were slightly cheaper while 20/21m were generally unchanged.
In crossbreds, 27m was slightly dearer, 28/30/31m were 0.5 percent dearer and 29m was unchanged.
In cardings, lambs and locks were generally unchanged, WI said.
WI said Japan and China were the principal buyers with strong support from local mills, Taiwan and Western Europe.
Of the 32,196 bales offered, 13.4 percent were passed in.
Sales continue next week in Goulburn, Melbourne and Fremantle with about 110,668 bales to be offered.
